original_title: EPA Administrator Lee Zeldin Rolls Back Clean Air Rules in Scott Pruitt-Style Purge

sources.title: EPA Launches Biggest Deregulatory Action in U.S. History
sources.access_notes: Official March 12, 2025 announcement lists 31 actions for reconsideration; it does not say those rule changes were already completed.

supported_facts.fact: EPA Administrator Lee Zeldin announced 31 deregulatory actions on March 12, 2025, including reconsideration of rules affecting power plants, vehicles, air pollution, and other areas.

unsupported_original_claims: The event occurred January 22, 2025, before Zeldin was confirmed as EPA administrator.
The March announcement itself completed all listed rollbacks.
The source establishes estimated tens of thousands of additional annual deaths, internal resignations, and legal challenges.
access_notes: The EPA release supports an announcement and reconsideration agenda on March 12, not completed regulatory rescissions on January 22. It does not support the claim’s mortality estimate or the details of internal dissent and lawsuits.
narrow_corrected_claim: On March 12, 2025, EPA Administrator Lee Zeldin announced 31 deregulatory actions, including reviews of air-pollution and vehicle rules.
exact_gap: The recorded date predates Zeldin’s confirmation; announcement/review must not be rewritten as completed rule repeal. Public-health impact and internal dissent require separate evidence.

original_title: Melania Trump NFT Collection Sells $45M+ Using White House Memorabilia

sources.title: Who Won the Melania Trump NFT Auction? Trump Crypto Wallet Linked to $185K Funds
sources.access_notes: Bloomberg reports on the January 2022 auction and a wallet trail; this supports a single auction transaction, not total collection sales.

supported_facts.fact: A January 2022 auction of Melania Trump’s “Head of State” NFT was reported at roughly $185,000, with Bloomberg tracing the winning transaction to a wallet linked to the project.

unsupported_original_claims: Melania’s collection earned more than $45 million in January 2022.
The Bloomberg investigation establishes that the entire collection was sold for $185,000 or that all funds originated from taxpayers.
The source establishes later Trump family NFT sales totals.
access_notes: Bloomberg reports on one auction/winning transaction of approximately $185,000; it does not establish $45 million in January 2022 collection revenue. The article’s wallet tracing raises a transaction-provenance question rather than proving the broad revenue claim.
narrow_corrected_title: Bloomberg reports roughly $185,000 Melania NFT auction
narrow_corrected_claim: Bloomberg investigated the roughly $185,000 winning bid for Melania Trump’s January 2022 “Head of State” NFT auction.
exact_gap: Replace the unsupported $45 million collection-sales claim with the documented individual auction and attribute the wallet link to Bloomberg; broader taxpayer-funding and later-sales assertions require separate sources.

original_title: Trump Entertainment Resorts Chapter 11: Fifth Bankruptcy, Employee Pensions Gutted (2009)

sources.title: Trump Entertainment Resorts Inc. Form 8-K, February 17, 2009
sources.access_notes: SEC filing is primary evidence of the Chapter 11 filing; it does not substantiate pension reductions.

supported_facts.fact: Trump Entertainment Resorts disclosed that the company and certain subsidiaries filed voluntary Chapter 11 petitions on February 17, 2009.

unsupported_original_claims: The 2009 restructuring reduced employee pension or benefit obligations for hundreds of workers as stated.
The source establishes all five bankruptcy events’ aggregate losses or that Trump personally avoided all financial losses.
access_notes: The SEC filing directly supports the February 17, 2009 Chapter 11 filing. It does not establish the employee-pension allegation or the broader cumulative-loss narrative, which remains unsupported by this source.
narrow_corrected_claim: Trump Entertainment Resorts and subsidiaries filed for Chapter 11 protection on February 17, 2009.
exact_gap: Keep the record to the filing unless separate documentation supports pension/benefit reductions and the other asserted consequences.

original_title: Trump Publicly Attacks Federal Judge as 'Radical Left Lunatic' After Court Block

sources.title: Chief Justice Roberts says calls for judges’ impeachment are inappropriate after Trump criticism
sources.access_notes: Reuters reports Trump’s March 18 attack on Judge James Boasberg and Chief Justice John Roberts’s response.

supported_facts.fact: On March 18, 2025, Trump called Judge James Boasberg a “radical left lunatic” and urged impeachment; Chief Justice John Roberts said impeachment was not an appropriate response to disagreement with a judicial decision.

unsupported_original_claims: The attack occurred on February 15, 2025.
Trump called the judge an “Obama hack” in the quoted episode (not established by this Reuters report).
The source establishes that the purpose was to intimidate the judiciary or that the remarks caused the pattern of later court blocks.
access_notes: The attack and Roberts response are dated March 18, not February 15. The report supports the specific insult and impeachment call, but motive/effect claims and the additional “Obama hack” quote need independent sourcing.
narrow_corrected_title: Trump attacks Judge Boasberg; Roberts rebukes impeachment calls
narrow_corrected_claim: Trump attacked Judge Boasberg and urged impeachment on March 18, 2025; Roberts responded that impeachment calls over judicial decisions were inappropriate.
exact_gap: Correct the event date and avoid asserting intimidation motive or broader effects as established facts.

original_title: Trump Fires Head of Office of Special Counsel, Eliminating Hatch Act Enforcement

sources.title: Trump v. Wilcox, Supreme Court order (24A790)
sources.publisher: Supreme Court of the United States
sources.access_notes: The order states Dellinger was removed on February 7 and records the district court’s temporary reinstatement; it does not find that OSC stopped functioning.

supported_facts.fact: The Supreme Court order records that Hampton Dellinger was removed as head of the Office of Special Counsel on February 7, 2025, and that a district court temporarily reinstated him during litigation.

unsupported_original_claims: Dellinger was fired January 20, 2025.
The removal eliminated OSC leadership or shut down Hatch Act and whistleblower enforcement.
A permanent final ruling on the removal’s legality is established by this order.
access_notes: The order supports a February 7 removal and temporary litigation relief. It does not show the OSC’s statutory functions ceased; the cited order is procedural and does not establish the claim’s broad enforcement consequences.
narrow_corrected_title: Hampton Dellinger removed as Office of Special Counsel head
narrow_corrected_claim: Hampton Dellinger was removed as Office of Special Counsel head on February 7, 2025; a district court temporarily reinstated him while the case proceeded.
exact_gap: Correct the date and avoid claiming that the OSC or its enforcement functions were eliminated. The legal outcome beyond the temporary procedural relief requires separate authority.

original_title: Trump Calls Saudi Arabia a 'Cash Cow' — Transactional Foreign Policy Exposed

sources.title: Trump defends Saudi arms sales amid Khashoggi crisis
sources.access_notes: AP reports Trump’s defense of Saudi arms sales and emphasis on U.S. jobs/business; the “cash cow” quotation was not verified.

supported_facts.fact: During the 2018 Khashoggi controversy, Trump defended U.S. arms sales to Saudi Arabia and emphasized their economic and employment value.

unsupported_original_claims: Trump called Saudi Arabia a “cash cow” in the October 11, 2018 episode.
The quote proves that U.S.-Saudi policy was purely transactional or that Saudi Arabia was thereby emboldened to act with impunity.
access_notes: AP supports Trump’s defense of arms sales amid the Khashoggi crisis, but the exact “cash cow” quote is not verified in the reviewed source. The source does not establish the broader foreign-policy philosophy or causal effects asserted.
narrow_corrected_title: Trump defends Saudi arms sales amid Khashoggi crisis
narrow_corrected_claim: Trump defended Saudi arms sales and emphasized their economic value during the Khashoggi crisis.
exact_gap: Do not retain the “cash cow” quotation unless a primary transcript or reliable contemporaneous source is found; keep interpretation attributed or omit it.

original_title: Trump Claims to Know More About Drones Than Anybody

sources.title: Remarks by President Trump at a Cabinet Meeting
sources.access_notes: Archived official transcript dates the remark January 2, 2019 and places it in a discussion about border security and a wall.

sources.title: Public Papers of the Presidents: Donald Trump, 2019, document 1
sources.access_notes: GovInfo transcript provides an official archival record of the same Cabinet meeting.

supported_facts.fact: On January 2, 2019, Trump said, “I know more about drones than anybody,” while arguing for a border wall and describing drones as a minor measure compared with the wall.

unsupported_original_claims: The statement was made in 2018.
Trump was discussing military targeting decisions or drone warfare in this passage.
Officials’ rejection of his technical expertise or operational harms are established by the transcript.
access_notes: The official transcript dates the remark to January 2, 2019, and its context is border security, not military targeting. The source does not support claims about classified programs, professional expertise, or operational consequences.
narrow_corrected_title: Trump says he knows more about drones during border-security debate
narrow_corrected_claim: Trump said he knew more about drones than anybody during a January 2, 2019 Cabinet discussion about border security.
exact_gap: Correct the year and context; omit unsupported claims about military operations, expert reactions, or consequences.

original_title: Russian Oligarchs Donated to Trump Inaugural Committee Through Straw Donors

sources.title: Political Donor Sentenced to 12 Years in Prison for Lobbying and Campaign Contribution Crimes, Tax Evasion
sources.access_notes: DOJ release covers Zuberi’s sentence and offenses; distinguish campaign contributions and foreign-agent conduct from a proven Russian-oligarch contribution to the inaugural fund.

sources.title: Trump donor charged with obstructing inauguration inquiry
sources.access_notes: AP reports the $900,000 inaugural contribution and the investigation’s allegations; allegations about funding sources are not established as a Russian-oligarch donation.

supported_facts.fact: Imaad Zuberi and his company Avenue Ventures contributed $900,000 to Trump’s 2017 inaugural committee; prosecutors investigated whether foreign nationals unlawfully funded the contribution, and Zuberi later pleaded guilty to obstructing that inquiry.
DOJ later described Zuberi’s criminal conduct involving illegal campaign contributions and unregistered foreign-agent activity.

unsupported_original_claims: Federal prosecutors or Senate investigators established that Russian oligarchs funded the $900,000 inaugural contribution through straw donors.
The sources establish the full scope of foreign funds in the inaugural committee.
Separate campaign-committee straw-donor allegations involving other individuals are evidence of this contribution’s source.
access_notes: The $900,000 donation and obstruction investigation are documented, but sources describe unresolved questions and alleged funding from other sources, including a Turkish-American businessman. Zuberi’s separate foreign-agent dealings involving a Ukrainian oligarch do not prove Russian oligarch money funded this inaugural donation.
narrow_corrected_title: Investigators examine Zuberi’s $900,000 Trump inaugural contribution
narrow_corrected_claim: Federal investigators examined the source of Imaad Zuberi’s $900,000 contribution to Trump’s 2017 inaugural committee; Zuberi later pleaded guilty to obstructing that inquiry.
exact_gap: No reviewed source establishes Russian oligarch funding of this inaugural contribution or the full scope of foreign money. Keep separate Zuberi’s distinct foreign-agent and campaign-finance conduct.

original_title: Rubio Shuts Down International Broadcasting — Voice of America Goes Dark

sources.title: Trump signs order to gut Voice of America, other agencies
sources.access_notes: Reuters attributes the order to Trump and reports the resulting reduction of USAGM/VOA operations; it does not attribute the action to Rubio.

sources.title: U.S. Agency for Global Media Complies with Presidential Executive Order to Reduce the Federal Bureaucracy
sources.access_notes: USAGM’s own announcement identifies implementation of the presidential order.

supported_facts.fact: Trump signed an executive order on March 14, 2025 directing a reduction of USAGM; USAGM announced compliance and VOA operations were sharply curtailed.

unsupported_original_claims: Secretary of State Marco Rubio shut down USAGM or personally took VOA off the air.
The action eliminated VOA permanently or eradicated all U.S. international broadcasting.
The source establishes the claimed propaganda victory or impact on authoritarian governments.
access_notes: The sources attribute the action to Trump’s executive order and USAGM’s implementation, not Rubio. They support a sharp operational curtailment, not claims about permanent abolition or foreign propaganda effects.
narrow_corrected_title: Trump order and USAGM actions curtail Voice of America
narrow_corrected_claim: Trump’s March 14 executive order prompted USAGM implementation that sharply curtailed Voice of America operations.
exact_gap: Correct the actor and distinguish operational curtailment from permanent abolition; any asserted international effect requires separate evidence.

original_title: Musk DOGE Fires Thousands of FDA Food Safety Inspectors

sources.title: U.S. FDA suspends food safety quality checks after staff cuts
sources.access_notes: Reuters reports suspension of certain FDA food-safety quality checks after staffing cuts; it does not support the asserted thousands of inspector firings or outbreak causation.

supported_facts.fact: Reuters reported in April 2025 that the FDA suspended certain food-safety quality checks after staffing cuts.

unsupported_original_claims: DOGE fired thousands of FDA food-safety inspectors in March 2025.
Foodborne outbreaks and recalls were caused by reduced inspection frequency following those firings.
The story supports a count of thousands of inspectors dismissed.
access_notes: The reported event is a suspension of quality checks after staffing reductions, not evidence that DOGE fired thousands of food inspectors. The cited report does not establish outbreak causation or the claimed inspector count.
narrow_corrected_title: FDA suspends food-safety quality checks after staff cuts
narrow_corrected_claim: Reuters reports FDA food-safety quality checks were suspended after staff cuts in April 2025.
exact_gap: Use the reported testing/check suspension as the discrete event; remove the unsupported inspector count, DOGE attribution, and causal outbreak claims.
